title: An AI system to help scientists write expert-level empirical software

mechanism.domainTask: LLM-guided generation and optimization of executable scientific software for scorable tasks
mechanism.populationDetail: An explicit PUCT search tree stores executable candidate programs as nodes with parent-child lineage and visit statistics.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate elite archive is described; the best-scoring node is selected from the maintained search tree at the end.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The tree is both the candidate population and the search-control structure; nodes are appended and selection pressure is applied through PUCT revisitation rather than deletion.
mechanism.generationDetail: One PUCT-selected parent/trial is broadly rewritten by the LLM into a complete executable code candidate; research ideas and prior method summaries are contextual references.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Sandbox execution scores, output logs, rank-normalized scores, and task-specific submetrics inform node ranking and later PUCT selection.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: At each iteration, PUCT selects one node from the full tree candidate set using rank score, visit count, prior, and exploration constant; the child is then generated from that node.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: PUCT tree statistics jointly serve as maintained population structure and parent-selection controller, while external research-idea injection and pairwise recombination operate as workflow-level guidance.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/An AI system to help scientists write expert-level empirical software.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: The current survey cites this paper primarily as a tree-structured population example and also describes a flat-population overlay; direct paper evidence supports tree structure, incremental insertion, broad unary rewriting, metadata feedback, adaptive PUCT control, and role-based multi-model use. Auxiliary Gemini calls should not be misread as same-step collaborative code generation.
